# Cedar of Payer Source (`cedar-of-payer-source`)

Checks that every nursing-home resident day has one proper payer: days with no payer, two payers on one day, payers not on your payer list, Medicare Part A past day 100, Part A coinsurance days with no secondary payer, hospice residents on Part A, and private pay with no responsible party. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Cedar never changes payers in PointClickCare or any other system.**

Evergreen ver 1 · Billing and revenue cycle · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`evergreen-core`](../evergreen-core)

```bash
npx -y cedar-of-payer-source demo
npx -y cedar-of-payer-source mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Cedar Hollow Health and Rehab, March 2026 (example coinsurance rate 200, not the CMS figure). Planted: Part A past day 100 (R301: 40 earlier days + Part A since 1 January), coinsurance days with no secondary payer (R302 from day 21), no payer for four days (R303), two payers from 20 March (R304), a payer spelled differently from the payer list (R305), a hospice resident on Part A (R306) and private pay with no responsible party (R307).

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `cedar_check` | List runs of resident days with a missing, doubled, unknown or improper payer for a month (or start to end). | runs |
| `cedar_write_report` | Write cedar-payer-source.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and cedar-payer-source.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/cedar). | runs |
| `cedar_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `cedar_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `cedar_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `cedar_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `census_update` | Cedar never changes payers in PointClickCare or any other system. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `cedar_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `census` (required) | Census export under --root (rows with resident, payer, from, to; the to day is not counted) |
| `residents` | Optional resident financial file under --root: secondary payer, responsible party, hospice agency, Part A days used earlier in the benefit period |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: your payer list and the daily coinsurance rate |
| `month` | Month to check, YYYY-MM |
| `start` | Start of the period (YYYY-MM-DD) if not a whole month |
| `end` | End of the period, inclusive |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx cedar-of-payer-source inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Census (`census`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Facility Name, Building, Location, Fac, Center |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Census Date |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `bed_status` | text | Bed Status, Status, Census Status, Action, Census Action, Leave Type |
| `room` | text | Room, Room Bed, Bed, Room/Bed, Unit |

### Resident financial file (`residents`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `secondary_payer` | text | Secondary Payer, Secondary, Secondary Insurance, Coinsurance Payer, Supplemental |
| `responsible_party` | text | Responsible Party, Guarantor, Financially Responsible, POA, Billing Contact |
| `hospice_agency` | text | Hospice, Hospice Agency, Hospice Provider |
| `part_a_days_used` | number | Part A Days Used, Prior SNF Days, Benefit Days Used |

## Settings file (`cedar_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `payers` | Your payer list (names as they appear on the census) |
| `coinsurance_rate` | Medicare SNF daily coinsurance for days 21-100 for the year (set it from the current CMS notice) |

## Memory

`cedar_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `cedar_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `payer_alias` | treats the alias as a known payer, so it is not flagged as unknown_payer. It never changes other checks. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `evergreen-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cedar-of-payer-source": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "cedar-of-payer-source",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add cedar-of-payer-source -- npx -y cedar-of-payer-source mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
cedar-of-payer-source tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
cedar-of-payer-source sources               # the columns each input is read from
cedar-of-payer-source inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
cedar-of-payer-source call cedar_check '{"census":"<census>"}'
cedar-of-payer-source eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
cedar-of-payer-source demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
